nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeCu-0.5 shows diffraction peaks at 44.5°, 51.8°, and 76.3° corresponding to the (111), (200), and (220) crystal planes of face-centered cubic (FCC) structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2b shows the XRD pattern of NiFeCu-0.5, where the diffraction peaks at 44.5°, 51.8°, and 76.3° correspond to the (111), (200), and (220) crystal planes of the face-centered cubic (FCC) structure.

properties.description: X-ray diffraction pattern showing diffraction rings

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu atomic ratio increases from 22.9% (NiFeCu-0) to 27.5% (NiFeCu-0.25) and 33.6% (NiFeCu-0.5) confirming magnetic field promoted Cu enrichment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To accurately quantify the elemental composition of NiFeCu-0, NiFeCu-0.25, and NiFeCu-0.5, the ICP-OES technique was used to analyze, and the results confirmed that the magnetic field promoted Cu enrichment on the NF surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeCu-0.5 has specific surface area of 40.86 m²/g, significantly higher than NiFeCu-0 (15.26 m²/g).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, BET tests show that the specific surface area of NiFeCu-0.5 (40.86 m² g⁻¹) is significantly higher than that of NiFeCu-0 (15.26 m² g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals lattice spacing of 0.21 nm corresponding to the (111) crystal plane of FCC structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM and HRTEM images (Figure 2f and Figure S15, Supporting Information) further reveal the lattice stripes, where the lattice spacing of 0.21 nm corresponds to the (111) crystal plane of the FCC structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern indicates NiFeCu-0.5 exhibits polycrystalline features with diffraction rings corresponding to (111), (200), (220), and (311) crystal planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Select area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern indicates that NiFeCu-0.5 exhibits polycrystalline features, with diffraction rings corresponding to the (111), (200), (220), and (311) crystal planes.

The high-resolution spectra of NiFeCu-0.5 Ni 2p... peaks at 869.7 and 852.7 eV correspond to Ni⁰; the peaks of 874.1 and 856.4 eV are attributed to Ni²⁺... Fe 2p spectrum, exhibiting bimodal peaks corresponding to Fe³⁺ (723.9 and 713.9 eV). Cu 2p spectra reveal... Cu⁰ (932.6 and 952.4 eV)... Cu²⁺ (934.8 eV and 954.9 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeCu-0.5 shows negative energy shifts at Ni K-edge and Fe K-edge indicating increased electron density around Ni and Fe sites; Cu K-edge shifts to higher energy indicating enhanced Cu oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiFeCu-0.5 exhibits a clear negative energy shift relative to NiFeCu, indicating that the magnetic-field-induced Cu enrichment raises the electron density around Ni sites. A comparable negative shift is observed at the Fe K-edge... the Cu K-edge of NiFeCu-0.5 shifts to high energy, which indicates that the oxidation state of Cu in NiFeCu-0.5 is enhanced.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Ni-Ni/Fe-Fe coordination at 2.2 Å and Cu-Cu at 2.5 Å for both catalysts; NiFeCu-0.5 shows weakened and right-shifted Cu-O peak at ~1.4 Å indicating reduced Cu-O coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier-transformed EXAFS spectra at the Ni K-edge reveal a dominant peak centered at 2.2 Å for both NiFeCu and NiFeCu-0.5... Fe K-edge exhibits an analogous feature near 2.2 Å corresponding to Fe-Fe bonding, while the Cu K-edge presents a distinct signature at 2.5 Å arising from Cu-Cu coordination... the Cu-O peak of NiFeCu-0.5 is obviously weakened and shifted to the right.
